title: Network Troubleshooting Tools
description: Master the command-line tools that diagnose connectivity, DNS, and latency problems.

data.text: When a web application slows down, times out, or returns errors, the root cause is almost always network-related. The difference between a junior and a senior engineer is often not the ability to write complex code, but the ability to quickly isolate whether the problem is DNS, routing, firewall rules, or application latency.

This lesson introduces the essential command-line tools every engineer should know. These utilities run on Windows, macOS, and Linux, and they reveal exactly what is happening between your device and the destination.

data.title: Diagnostic Commands
items: ping — tests basic reachability and measures round-trip time.
traceroute / tracert — shows every hop between source and destination.
nslookup / dig — inspects DNS records for a domain.
netstat / ss — lists open ports and active connections on a machine.
curl / wget — makes HTTP requests and shows headers, timing, and body.
telnet / nc — tests TCP connectivity to a specific host and port.
tcpdump / Wireshark — captures and analyzes raw network packets.

data.text: Ping sends an ICMP Echo Request to a destination and measures how long the Echo Reply takes to return. It tells you whether a host is reachable and gives you a rough idea of latency. However, ICMP is often blocked by firewalls, so a failed ping does not always mean the host is down.

data.title: Ping a Destination
data.content: Measure round-trip time to a remote host.
data.code:
ping google.com

PING google.com (142.250.80.46): 56 data bytes
64 bytes from 142.250.80.46: icmp_seq=0 ttl=115 time=12.4 ms
64 bytes from 142.250.80.46: icmp_seq=1 ttl=115 time=11.8 ms

data.text: Traceroute reveals the path packets take through the internet. It sends probes with increasing Time-To-Live values and listens for ICMP Time Exceeded messages from each router along the way. The output shows every hop, the router's IP, and the latency to that point.

data.title: Pro Tip: MTR
data.text: On Linux and macOS, mtr combines ping and traceroute into a single continuous diagnostic tool. It refreshes in real time, making it easier to spot intermittent packet loss at a specific hop.

curl is more than a file downloader. With the right flags, it shows exactly how a server responds: DNS lookup time, TLS handshake time, time-to-first-byte, and total transfer time. It also lets you inspect headers, follow redirects, and test different HTTP methods.

data.title: Diagnose HTTP Timing with cURL
data.content: Measure DNS, connect, TLS, and transfer times for an HTTPS request.
data.code:
curl -o /dev/null -s -w "\n\
  DNS: %{time_namelookup}s\n\
  Connect: %{time_connect}s\n\
  TLS: %{time_appconnect}s\n\
  First Byte: %{time_starttransfer}s\n\
  Total: %{time_total}s\n" \
  https://example.com

data.text: netstat and ss show which ports your machine is listening on and which remote connections are active. ss is the modern replacement for netstat on Linux and is significantly faster on systems with many connections. Use these tools to verify that your web server is actually listening on port 80 or 443, or to identify unexpected open ports.

data.title: List Listening Sockets
data.content: Show all listening TCP ports and the processes using them.
data.code:
# Linux with ss
ss -tulnp

# Windows with netstat
netstat -ano | findstr :443

items.question: Why does ping work but curl time out?
items.answer: ICMP may be allowed while TCP is blocked by a firewall. Some hosts disable ICMP entirely for security, so a successful ping is not a guarantee that HTTP ports are open.

items.question: Why is traceroute showing asterisks on some hops?
items.answer: Asterisks mean the router at that hop did not return an ICMP response. This is often due to rate limiting or firewall rules, not necessarily packet loss. Look at the next hop that does respond to identify where delay increases.

items.question: What is the difference between netstat and ss?
items.answer: ss is the modern replacement for netstat on Linux. It reads from kernel memory directly, making it much faster and more accurate on systems with thousands of connections.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: ping tests reachability and latency, but ICMP is often blocked.
traceroute reveals the path and identifies slow or dropping hops.
curl provides detailed HTTP timing and header inspection.
ss and netstat expose local port and connection state.
data.takeaway: Systematic troubleshooting starts with these tools. Use them to eliminate layers one by one: DNS, routing, firewall, TLS, and application.
